newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic in Virginia pact with MCI.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic in Virginia pact with MCI.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp. said Monday its Bell Atlantic-Virginia subsidiary has entered into a pact with the local service affiliate of MCI Communications Corp. to connect their networks in the state.

It would be the first comprehensive interconnection and resale agreement between a Bell Atlantic company and a major long distance phone company under legislation last year allowing long distance carriers to compete for local business.
The seven Bell Atlantic operating companies have now reached 58 comprehensive interconnection agreements with 18 competing local exchange companies, Bell Atlantic said.
Under the pact, MCI will be able to connect its facilities with portions of Bell Atlantic's network to provide local exchange telephone services in competition with Bell Atlantic.
The Philadelphia-based company said the pact also allows MCI to buy local dialtone service from Bell Atlantic at wholesale prices and resell it to customers.
In addition, the pact covers details as to how the companies will physically connect their networks and the price to be paid for completion of calls on each other's networks.
The agreement is subject to approval by Virginia's State Corporation Commission.
Bell Atlantic cannot offer long distance in its service area until it complies with a 14-point checklist prescribed by the federal Telecommunications Act.
Bell Atlantic's stock fell 87.5 cents to $75.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading. MCI was barely changed at $39.188 on Nasdaq.
